findings.claim: §12.7.5 'Full de-adoption' step 2 provides a PATCH example payload of {"strict": true, "contexts": []} (empty array) while the comment immediately above says 'pass the remaining contexts you want to keep.' An adopter who has other required-check contexts alongside the SCP-federation one, and who copies the example payload literally without substituting their non-SCP contexts, will issue a PATCH that removes ALL required status checks from their branch protection — not just the SCP-federation context.
findings.evidence: ADOPT-001 §12.7.5 Full de-adoption step 2 comment at the PATCH invocation: '# Remove the SCP-federation context (replace OWNER/NAME/BRANCH; pass the remaining contexts you want to keep)'. Immediately below, the example payload body reads '{"strict": true, "contexts": []}'. The preceding list step instructs 'gh api .../required_status_checks --jq .contexts' to enumerate current contexts, but the PATCH body uses [] rather than the populated array-minus-SCP pattern implied by the comment. For WP-SCP-024 estate-cascade targets (CT, FLA, PIM, recommender, shopify-app, mapp-doc-agent) that may carry non-SCP required checks alongside the SCP-federation context, applying the example literally silently removes all required-check enforcement from main. The section's stated goal is to foreclose partial de-adoption (deleting wrapper without removing the required-check leaves branch unmergeable); this gap inverts the risk — an operator who removes more than intended is a different accidental partial state.
findings.impact: Low for SCP self-dogfood (SCP's main has only one required check). Moderate for WP-SCP-024 estate cascade repos that may have pre-existing CI required checks. The preceding list command mitigates by giving the operator visibility into current contexts, but the example payload and its accompanying comment are internally inconsistent, creating a trap for operators who copy-paste without adjusting. Does not block this PR's merge since the underlying closure of COMP-MAJ-005 (Full de-adoption section exists) is genuine; the gap is a documentation clarity issue.
findings.mitigation: In the next ADOPT-001 maintenance pass (020H.1 planning pass or v1.1), update the PATCH example to show the explicit substitution case: {"strict": true, "contexts": ["<other-required-check-1>"]} and add a one-sentence inline note: 'If the SCP federation context was your only required check, pass an empty array; if you have other required checks, include them here or the PATCH will remove them.' Alternatively, show two code blocks — the single-check case (contexts: []) and the multi-check case. No descoping — Full de-adoption section is correct in structure; this is a code-example clarity fix only.

findings.claim: FIX-ROUND-2.md claims COMP-MIN-002 ('SCP-CODEOWNERS ambiguity') is 'closed implicitly by the §12.7.4 rewrite.' The claim is inaccurate. §12.7.4 Gate 1 still uses the backtick-formatted `SCP-CODEOWNERS` label — the specific surface the R1 reviewer identified as causing adopters to misread Gate 1 as requiring approval from @jrnb2024 (SCP's own CODEOWNER) rather than from the adopter's own CODEOWNERS. The parenthetical clarification was added but the label was not removed as the R1 mitigation specified.
findings.evidence: ADOPT-001 §12.7.4 Gate 1 current text (lines 895–898): 'Approving review from a member of `SCP-CODEOWNERS` (your repo's CODEOWNERS for paths matching the gate's domain — typically `services.yml`, `output/findings/waivers.json`, or `policies/**` if you mirror locally).' FIX-ROUND-2.md closure description: 'Closed implicitly by the §12.7.4 rewrite — the new wording (your repo's CODEOWNERS for paths matching the gate's domain) clarifies the meaning.' Update the closure note in DISPATCH-NOTE to reflect that COMP-MIN-002 remains open pending this edit — do not mark it closed in any subsequent STATUS.md tracked-forward entry until the label is removed. self_reported_concerns: All seven MAJ closures were verified by direct reading of the current ADOPT-001 and STATUS.md file contents against the closure claims in FIX-ROUND-2.md. All seven are textually faithful and not fabricated or approximated. The COMP-MAJ-001+002 closure collapses both findings into a single one-line edit in §11.10 as the FIX-ROUND-2.md describes — this is a legitimate combined closure since both findings traced to the same sentence.

COMP-MAJ-004 API syntax: the gh api endpoint /branches/BRANCH/protection/required_status_checks returns a JSON object with both legacy .contexts (array of strings) and newer .checks (array of objects with context + app_id). The verification command uses --jq '{strict: .strict, contexts: .contexts}' which is syntactically correct for the v3 REST API. However, if enable-required-check.sh wrote the required check using the newer checks format (with app_id), the legacy .contexts field in the response may return empty while .checks holds the actual context. This is a known GitHub API evolution issue outside the scope of this doc patch but adopters using the verification command should be aware they may need --jq .checks[].context on newer GitHub API versions.

COMP-MAJ-005 PATCH endpoint: gh api -X PATCH .../protection/required_status_checks with --input - and a JSON body containing {"strict": true, "contexts": []} is syntactically valid per the GitHub REST API v3. The PATCH endpoint accepts both the legacy contexts array and the newer checks array. Using contexts: [] is consistent with how enable-required-check.sh sets the required check (it also uses the contexts format in its PUT payload per D-035). The PATCH-contexts vs PUT-contexts parity means the removal procedure is mechanically consistent with the setup procedure — no format mismatch.

Cross-document convergence confirmed: ADOPT-001 §12.7.4 single-operator mode references D-033 for the count=0 rationale (GitHub forbids PR self-review). The bus-factor-1 disclosure paragraph references D-031 for SCP's own single-operator governance (CODEOWNERS personal-account path). These are different decisions covering different concerns and are correctly cited. D-033 explains the branch-protection review-count correction; D-031 explains the CODEOWNERS governance mode. No circularity.

COMP-MIN-001 deferral note: the GitHub sequencing constraint (an adopter must merge at least one PR with the wrapper active before running enable-required-check.sh, because GitHub only accepts context names that exist in the repo's check history) is not stated anywhere in §12.7. The §12.7.3 verification step 3 (draft PR) implicitly assumes the wrapper is already merged, but the ordering dependency is not made explicit. This remains the open gap from COMP-MIN-001 and the deferral to v1.1 is accepted — it is non-blocking but should be included in the v1.1 §12.7 setup-sequence paragraph when that work is done.
